answers.reason: Chalcis is identified with Anjar; none of the candidates denotes that settlement. Salamis, Chios and the listed Israelite towns have different locations.
Charmande is identified with Hit on the Euphrates. None of the candidates shares that identification; Haran is Harran and Kartan is Khirbet el Qureiyeh.
Eridu is the Mesopotamian settlement at Tell Abu Shahrain. None of the candidates denotes that site; even the Babylonian Cherub has no evidence identifying it with Eridu.
Etruria is a region of Italy. It is geographically distinct from Persia and from the Judean settlement Beth-zur.
Gath-padalla is identified with Jett, whereas Gadara is Umm Qais. These are separate settlements, with no evidence of an alternate-name relationship.
Gergesa at Kursi and Gerasa at Jerash are separate settlements. Variant Gospel readings involving Gergesenes and Gerasenes do not make those towns the same referent.
Gutium is a Mesopotamian/Zagros region. Gittaim is a settlement in Israel, and Rhegium is Reggio Calabria in Italy.

Halahha denotes the settlement identified with Al Abbasiyah. The supplied Halah record denotes a wider area about 60 km around Halahha, so geographic association does not establish identical referents.

Harhar is identified with Nahavand. The closest candidate, Hara in 1 Chronicles 5:26, is explicitly represented here as a generic expression for mountains or cities, with no identification with Nahavand.
Hatti denotes the historical Hittite land or region. None of the candidates denotes that region; Attalia, Jattir and Hamath are separate settlements.
